chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman from al-Husayn ibn Sadir from his father from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The drinker of wine will come on the Day of Resurrection with his face blackened, his tongue protruding, his saliva dripping onto his chest. It is a right of Allah, the Exalted, to give him drink from the Well of Khabal.
I asked, 'And what is the Well of Khabal?' He said, 'A well in which the pus of the fornicators flows.'
ai.seo_question: What is the physical description of a wine drinker on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the physical manifestations of drunkenness in this world are mirrored by specific bodily afflictions in the Hereafter, emphasizing the concept of *haqq* (a due right) for Allah to punish the drinker with the 'Well of Khabal.' This well, defined as containing the pus of fornicators, highlights the connection between wine consumption and sexual immorality, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence linking the two major sins. The description serves as a vivid eschatological warning, illustrating how the internal corruption of the drinker becomes externally visible on the Day of Judgment.
